nodes.label: JWT Secret & Cookie Configuration
nodes.rationale: JWT lives in an HttpOnly cookie whose name, expiry and refresh expiry are injected into erd-core via SPRING_APPLICATION_JSON, which is why the browser side never stores a bearer token itself.

nodes.label: Sidebar / Router Shell Layout
nodes.rationale: The sidebar is suppressed on the login and register routes by isLoginOrRegister(), so authentication screens render full-bleed while every authenticated route gets the collapsible chrome.

nodes.label: PK/UN/NN/AI Constraint Toggles
nodes.rationale: The Not-Null checkbox binds to the inverse of item.nullable and is disabled whenever the attribute is a primary key or auto-increment, because those already imply NOT NULL and letting the user clear it would emit invalid DDL.

nodes.label: Dual Datastore Split (Postgres + Mongo)
nodes.rationale: Relational data (users, projects, membership) lives in PostgreSQL while diagram documents live in MongoDB, so the diagram payload can evolve without schema migrations.

nodes.label: Coverage Regression Gate
nodes.rationale: Unit tests with coverage run before the build so a coverage regression fails fast, and the report is uploaded with if:always() so a failing run still yields a diagnosable artifact.

nodes.label: strictTemplates Enforcement Gate
nodes.rationale: The build step is kept last because the karma builder runs with aot:false, so `ng build` is the only step that actually enforces strictTemplates against the component templates.

nodes.label: Full-Stack Docker Compose Workflow
nodes.rationale: Compose is the recommended local path because the app is only meaningful alongside erd-core, PostgreSQL and MongoDB; a cached Maven volume keeps rebuild cost down after the slow first build.

nodes.label: GoJS Interactive Diagramming
nodes.rationale: GoJS was chosen as the diagram engine because ER diagrams need interactive node/link editing, hit-testing and templated rendering that a plain SVG/canvas layer would have to reimplement.

nodes.label: SockJS/StompJS Realtime Transport
nodes.rationale: STOMP over SockJS is used for server communication so multiple editors can receive diagram mutations pushed from erd-core rather than polling for changes.

nodes.label: GHCR Image Publish Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Images are tagged both :latest and :${{ github.sha }} on every push to main so a deploy can be pinned to an exact commit, with GitHub Actions cache (type=gha) reused across builds.

nodes.label: Role Badge (OWNER/EDITOR/VIEWER)
nodes.rationale: The badge always renders the role while the edit/remove actions are gated on isOwner(), so every member can see the permission structure but only the owner can change it.

nodes.label: Relationship Cardinality Toolbar
nodes.rationale: 1:1, 1:N and N:N are picked as a mode before two tables are clicked, so the cardinality is known up front and N:N can materialise an intermediary entity rather than a plain link.

nodes.label: Role-Gated Editing Toolbar
nodes.rationale: VIEWER users get a reduced toolbar that keeps export but drops add, import and relationship tools, so read-only access is expressed in the UI rather than only rejected by the server.

nodes.label: Owner-Only Project Delete
nodes.rationale: The delete control is rendered only when isOwnerOfProject(project) holds, so ownership is enforced in the template as well as by the backend, keeping non-owners from seeing an action that would fail.

nodes.label: Three-Table ER Motif
nodes.rationale: The mark encodes the product itself: two parent tables joined through a diamond into a third table - the N:N relationship with an intermediary entity that the diagram editor materialises.

nodes.label: Collaboration Status Bar
nodes.rationale: The status bar surfaces the viewer role and every active entity lock so a second editor understands why a table is unclickable before they try to open it.
